## RhoGAM Boy

Hi, I'm Suyeong. I owe my life to an antibody. As the second child of an Rh(D)-negative mother, I would not have been born safely without RhoGAM, an antibody therapy.

That story led me to pharmacy, and then to immunology. I completed my Pharm.D. at Seoul National University and an M.S. in immunology at the same school, and I am now a first-year PhD student in immunology at UT Southwestern.

The name of this blog, 'GAMRho', is the name of a therapy I hope to create one day. Just as RhoGAM saved me, I want to help protect lives like mine by developing 'GAMRho'. This blog will follow my journey toward that therapy, along with my many other interests.

## Research interests

Some antibodies save lives, while others attack our own bodies. I want to study where pathogenic autoantibodies, and the immunological origins that produce them, come from, through the lens of genetics.

- **Inherited?** Which genetic factors contribute to the emergence of pathogenic immune clones?
- **Selected?** How do T cell development and immune tolerance in the thymus give rise to autoreactive antibodies?
- **Expanded?** Which clones expand through the somatic changes that come with age?
